original_annotations: Use a butter knife to scoop nut butter from the jar. [54.270, 71.843]; error: Used a spoon instead of a butter knife.
Spread nut butter onto the tortilla. [73.947, 128.243]; error: Used a spoon instead of a butter knife.

observed_events.description: The wearer retrieves and opens the jar. At V0:3 a metal spoon is held edge-on beside the lid; continuous frames establish that same spoon turns face-on and changes hands.
The same spoon scoops nut butter. No knife-to-spoon exchange is established.

supported_claims.text: The metal utensil by the jar lid at V0:3 is viewed edge-on. V1 reveals the same concave spoon and shows it scooping nut butter. Its physical referent does not change.

construct.research_question: Can an Agent preserve the selected utensil when its later view and use clarify the same object?
construct.belief_before: The held utensil is a spoon seen edge-on; do not infer a different physical knife.
construct.belief_after: The same spoon turns face-on and is used in the jar.
construct.required_behavior_change: Retain a practical ordinary spoon as the view clarifies it.
construct.no_update_failure: Retaining a legal spoon is correct; a knife is a mistaken category hypothesis, not an ignored physical swap.
construct.overupdate_failure: Replace the legal spoon with another utensil or add a second listing.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: Words alone cannot identify the held utensil. V0 supplies its reference; V1 reveals the same spoon bowl and use.

task_blueprint.instruction: I want a spare like the table utensil I am holding while opening the nut-butter jar. Add one listing that supplies that kind of utensil for scooping spreads. Size, handle decoration and pack size can differ.

observed.why: Same edge-on utensil reveals its concave bowl. Knife alternative is a category hypothesis, not a separately observed replaced object.
